content.prompt:
Thales’ theorem states that: An angle in a semicircle is a right angle.

This question develops two other proofs of Thales’ theorem. We must prove, in each part, that $\angle APB=90^\circ$.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
(Euclid’s proof) Join $PO$, and produce $AP$ to $X$.

Let $\angle A=\alpha$ and $\angle B=\beta$.

spec.description: Diameter AB and chords AP, PB; dashed red constructions PO and PX, with A, P, X collinear. Ordinary geometry and point marker use house black.
spec.mathematics: O is the centre; A,O,B are collinear; A,P,X are collinear; alpha=PAB and beta=PBA.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Prove that $\angle APB=\alpha+\beta$, and that $\angle XPB=\alpha+\beta$.

answer.short:
$\angle APB=\angle XPB=\alpha+\beta$.

Use equal base angles in the two isosceles triangles and the exterior-angle theorem.
answer.worked:
$OA=OP$, so $\triangle AOP$ is isosceles and $\angle APO=\angle PAO=\alpha$.

$OB=OP$, so $\triangle BOP$ is isosceles and $\angle OPB=\angle PBO=\beta$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle APB&=\angle APO+\angle OPB\\\angle APB&=\alpha+\beta.\end{align*}$$
Since $AP$ is produced to $X$, the exterior-angle theorem in $\triangle APB$ gives
$$\begin{align*}\angle XPB&=\angle PAB+\angle PBA\\\angle XPB&=\alpha+\beta.\end{align*}$$

answer.short: $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$, since the equal adjacent angles at $P$ form a straight angle.
answer.worked:
$A,P,X$ are collinear, so $\angle APB+\angle XPB=180^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}2(\alpha+\beta)&=180^\circ\\\alpha+\beta&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\angle APB=90^\circ$.

spec.description: Diameter AB and triangle APB, with dashed red diameter PM through O. Ordinary geometry and point marker use house black.
spec.mathematics: O is the centre; A,O,B and P,O,M are collinear; alpha=PAB and beta=PBA.

answer.short:
$\angle AOM=2\alpha$ and $\angle BOM=2\beta$.

Use equal radii and the exterior-angle theorem.
answer.worked:
$OA=OP$, so $\angle OAP=\angle APO=\alpha$.

$OB=OP$, so $\angle OBP=\angle BPO=\beta$.

Since $PO$ is produced to $M$, the exterior-angle theorem gives
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOM&=\angle OAP+\angle APO\\\angle AOM&=2\alpha,\\\angle BOM&=\angle OBP+\angle BPO\\\angle BOM&=2\beta.\end{align*}$$

$A,O,B$ are collinear, so $\angle AOM+\angle MOB=180^\circ$.

Substituting the results from part iii gives $2\alpha+2\beta=180^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}2\alpha+2\beta&=180^\circ\\\alpha+\beta&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The equal base angles give $\angle APB=\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$.
